matt_h: Quick sanity check — brought KiteBench-9B (baseline fp16 -> int6) through the usual smoke. Unit econ looks promising but we see a regression on multi-paragraph summarization slices (>512 tokens).
sara_p: Nice. Can you drop the perf + cost numbers?
matt_h: Sure — perf: 1.9K tokens/s p99 on batch=8, latency median 85ms. Cost: ~0.018 $/1k tokens (hosted pricing equivalent) for int6 vs 0.037 for fp16. So ~52% token-cost savings.
vivek_r: That cost delta is huge. Where is the quality hit?
matt_h: On our GTN summary slice (customer-style), ROUGE-L down ~6 points vs fp16 and some hallucination rate up on factuality checks. Short-turn chat looks fine. Longform recall drops primarily when the model needs to cite long context (>512).
sara_p: Hmm. Is this difference concentrated in specific prompts or universal across topics?
matt_h: Mostly universal on long-form extraction and citation tasks. Multi-turn summarization with referential pronouns breaks more often.
jen_ops: Any log/stack traces or runtime anomalies? Could be KV-cache or kvc compaction bug.
matt_h: No runtime errors — KV hit rates look normal. Quantization map looks correct. I ran a quick kalibr (per-layer) diff and layers 22-24 show slightly higher activation variance after quant.
kyle_prod: From product POV we care about user-visible regressions. If short chat is fine but longform breaks, we can route longform to fp16 fallback for now. What's the cost/impact of routing 20% traffic to fp16?
matt_h: If longform is ~18% of tokens, routing those to fp16 raises average cost to ~0.028 $/1k tokens (so ~24% savings vs all-fp16).
vivek_r: Could we do a hybrid: int6 for prefix/fast tokens, fp16 for final decoding? Any runtime support?
jen_ops: We have partial support for mixed-precision decode routing but would need an intermediate fallback policy. Workload-aware routing would add ~10ms overhead.
sara_p: Before we change infra, can we try a targeted per-layer recalibration? Maybe bias correction or folding for layers 22-24.
matt_h: Plan: 1) run per-layer bias-correction patch, 2) rerun the GTN longform slice (5k samples), 3) measure ROUGE / hallucination F1 and unit econ. I can take 1+2 today.
ci-bot: Pipeline queued: kitebench-int6-recal-1765009999 (estimated run 45m) :rocket:

kyle_prod: If recalibrating brings ROUGE loss to <=2 points we can recommend int6 with longform fallback as an interim. Otherwise recommend holding on int6 for GTN until further model-level tuning.
vivek_r: Also capture synthetic QA deltas and log worst-case prompts for product to consider guardrails.
matt_h: Will attach the patch + sample diffs in the formal handoff doc after the run. Quick ask: product, do we want a communications plan if we flip to int6 with fallback?
kyle_prod: Yes — short note to GTN with performance + expected 20% savings and a heads-up about rare longform citations degrading, listing fallback behavior.
sara_p: Great. After the run, let's meet 30m to decide rollout flags.
matt_h: On it. Posting results here in ~50m. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
